title: Universal Controller Update
summary: HOTAS BF6 v2.0.0 is the first major architecture expansion of the project, generalizing the physical-input layer from a T.Flight-oriented workflow into persistent universal DirectInput controller management. It adds a durable multi-device registry, automatic low-frequency controller discovery, explicit controller selection and verification, per-device calibration and vJoy requirement memory, ambiguity-safe reconnect and switching behavior, a new Overview dashboard, stronger HidHide self-access handling, system-tray operation, controller-specific troubleshooting/reset tools, in-app uninstall access, and a more unified Settings/controller-management experience while keeping discovery, persistence, UI, setup, repair, and tray work outside the low-latency DirectInput-to-vJoy report path.
statusNote: DEPRECATED: v2.0.0 contains a launch-blocking startup defect in the new system-tray integration. The tray menu can initialize under QGuiApplication even though the Qt Widgets tray path requires QApplication, causing the mapper to exit during startup instead of opening and running normally. Do not install or use v2.0.0. Upgrade to v2.0.1 or newer, which corrects the startup object and strengthens packaged Qt Widgets and upgrade-path validation.
highlights: Generalizes the mapper from a primarily T.Flight-oriented physical-input workflow into a persistent universal DirectInput controller platform without moving controller-management work into the report-processing hot path.

Adds a persistent verified-controller registry with layered HID, DirectInput, product, vendor/product, and capability identity matching so known hardware can be recognized across reconnects and restarts.

Stores controller-specific calibration, remembered vJoy capability requirements, verification state, and offline device memory per physical device instead of allowing setup data to leak between unrelated controllers.
Adds low-frequency DirectInput inventory and arrival/removal discovery that tracks attached physical controllers while explicitly excluding vJoy from physical input selection.

Adds an Input Controllers / Controller Manager experience that shows connected, verified, new, active, and remembered-offline devices together and supports refresh, setup/verification, active-device selection, and forgetting remembered hardware.
Uses ambiguity-safe controller matching: identical or insufficiently distinguishable devices are not silently selected, preventing automatic binding to the wrong physical controller.

Known healthy controllers can reconnect quietly, while newly discovered controllers enter the themed Verify Setup flow only when selection, calibration, readiness, or verification actually requires user attention.

Adds optional intelligent controller switching that only auto-selects when exactly one eligible verified device is unambiguous, preserving explicit user selection when multiple plausible devices exist.

Adds a new Overview landing page summarizing the active physical controller, vJoy output, setup/readiness health, current configuration, mapping state, and presentation-smoothed performance metrics while Diagnostics remains the raw engineering view.
Improves HidHide handling with explicit detection of mapper self-access blocking, including cases where HidHide can prevent the physical controller from appearing to the app at all.

Adds a narrow HidHide allowlist-only repair path and installer-time registration of the installed mapper executable where permitted, while preserving unrelated HidHide application and hidden-device entries.
Adds native system-tray operation with controlled close-to-tray behavior and a concise tray menu so the mapper can remain available without occupying the main window.

Adds controller-only troubleshooting/reset tools so broken controller setup state can be cleared without indiscriminately deleting profiles, mappings, curves, Automation, or unrelated application configuration.
Adds an in-app uninstaller entry and safer uninstall defaults that retain shared dependencies and user data unless the user deliberately chooses otherwise.

Standardizes controller/setup controls inside Settings so controller selection, readiness, verification, troubleshooting, HidHide/vJoy status, and related maintenance actions are presented as one coherent workflow.

Keeps controller discovery, registry persistence, setup/readiness inspection, HidHide work, tray behavior, Overview smoothing, and uninstall/reset operations outside the DirectInput-to-vJoy report loop so the existing low-latency mapper architecture remains isolated.

title: Startup & Upgrade Hotfix
summary: Fixes a launch-blocking issue introduced in v2.0.0 where the system-tray menu could initialize under QGuiApplication instead of the required QApplication. v2.0.1 also strengthens packaged Qt Widgets validation and the v1.9.3 to v2 upgrade acceptance path while preserving existing configuration and mapper performance.
statusNote: Startup and upgrade hotfix; upgrade to v2.0.2 for dashboard, settings, tray, and controller-switching polish.
highlights: Replaces the mapper's QGuiApplication startup object with QApplication for the existing Qt Widgets tray menu.
Fails packaging when Qt6Widgets.dll is absent and adds deterministic Widgets/tray-menu startup coverage.
Validates clean install, v1.9.3 schema-14 upgrade, already-migrated schema-15 recovery, and the published built-in updater chain.
Logs an immediate mapper startup exit as a failed launch handoff rather than treating installer success as complete update success.
Preserves Universal Controller Update behavior, user profiles, curves, mappings, buttons, POVs, Automation, preferences, and the mapper hot path.

title: Dashboard & UX Polish
summary: v2.0.2 gives the Universal Controller Update the interface it deserves, with a redesigned Overview dashboard, standardized Settings experience, polished theme-aware tray controls, and a permanent global mapping control. It also completes per-controller vJoy requirement enforcement during device switching and hardens new-device verification when multiple controllers are connected.
statusNote: Dashboard and UX polish release; upgrade to v2.0.3 for multi-controller setup and vJoy reliability fixes.
highlights: Replaces the card-stack Overview with a signal-flow dashboard for physical input, HOTAS BF6 processing, vJoy output, health, capability, and smoothed performance state.
Places the theme-aware mapping state and Start or Stop action permanently in the main header and removes the Axis-page duplicate.
Reorganizes Settings into aligned responsive sections and separates maintenance from the confirmation-protected uninstaller.
Applies Legacy, Standard, and Top Gun visual tokens to the existing reliable Qt tray menu.
Validates saved target vJoy requirements during controller switching, preserves adequate existing output supersets, and blocks mapping restoration until valid output is available.
Explicitly acquires and verifies a selected new controller regardless of another controller's connection state.

title: Multi-Controller Setup & vJoy Reliability Hotfix
summary: HOTAS BF6 v2.0.3 hardens the Universal Controller workflow using real multi-controller hardware testing. It fixes incorrect setup targeting when a new controller is connected, completes NEW-to-VERIFIED persistence after automatic repair, ensures vJoy capacity is actually sufficient for each verified controller, makes disconnected devices visually unmistakable, cleans generic controller terminology, and fixes remaining Settings layout and styling regressions.
statusNote: Multi-controller reliability hotfix; upgrade to v2.0.4 for the UI responsiveness fix.
highlights: Removes the mapper-ownership shortcut that treated a BUSY vJoy device with successful reports as sufficient without validating axes, buttons, and POV capacity.
Configures and reinspects the actual selected vJoy device before setup can become Ready, including the safe first-time physical button-capacity floor and saved controller-specific requirements.
Carries explicit DirectInput controller identity from new-device discovery into a themed setup selector, so a newly connected controller never opens verification for an already active controller.
Completes post-repair validation by immediately saving or updating the selected controller, clearing NEW and preserving VERIFIED after the setup popup closes.
Distinguishes active connected, selected offline, verified, new, and offline saved controllers; adds an intentional zero-connected state and clear automatic-switch feedback.
Repairs compact Settings-row text layout, fully themes the vJoy +/- selector and theme menu controls, and uses Controller or Device terminology for generic physical inputs.

Keeps Universal Controller discovery, registry persistence, readiness inspection, verification, driver transactions, UI rendering, and all new state handling outside the DirectInput-to-vJoy report loop.

title: UI Responsiveness Hotfix
summary: Fixes a severe UI responsiveness regression where broad high-frequency state notifications caused expensive controller and device presentation work to be repeatedly reevaluated. v2.0.4 separates telemetry from controller and configuration state, caches controller presentation data, and restores smooth responsiveness without changing the mapper hot path.
statusNote: UI responsiveness hotfix; upgrade to v2.0.5 for published updater acceptance reliability.
highlights: Replaces the 16 ms broad state notification with dedicated input and telemetry notifications, so slow Settings and controller bindings stay idle while live metrics remain responsive.
Caches the controller presentation model behind a dedicated controllersChanged notification and only publishes a replacement after a material change.
Compares low-frequency DirectInput inventory snapshots before matching or rebuilding the controller model, leaving unchanged discovery ticks quiet.
Uses one Settings-page controller-model reference and a cached connected-controller count rather than repeatedly calling the C++ controller property in QML loops.
Adds focused notification/cache contract coverage and a ten-second steady-state controller-model validation while preserving DirectInput discovery cadence and mapper behavior.

title: Published Updater Acceptance Hotfix
summary: HOTAS BF6 v2.0.5 fixes the headless GitHub Actions environment used to validate the public v1.9.3 built-in updater path. It preserves v2.0.4 UI responsiveness behavior and all shipped mapper code while making the isolated acceptance launch the updated Qt application with the same offscreen platform used by existing installer smoke tests.
statusNote: Published updater acceptance hotfix; upgrade to v2.0.6 for public latest-manifest readiness validation.
highlights: Sets the Qt offscreen platform only inside the isolated published-updater acceptance so the v1.9.3 launcher, helper, installer, updated launcher, and updated mapper can be exercised on a non-interactive GitHub-hosted Windows runner.
Leaves user installs, normal desktop mapper startup, controller input, vJoy output, and the DirectInput-to-vJoy report path unchanged.
Emits the updater log on an acceptance startup failure, making a future public-update handoff failure diagnosable from its CI receipt.

title: Published Manifest Readiness Hotfix
summary: HOTAS BF6 v2.0.6 fixes a release-acceptance race in which GitHub could publish a release before its public latest-manifest alias advanced. The v1.9.3 updater acceptance now waits for the exact latest endpoint that the shipped launcher consumes to identify the expected release before exercising the unchanged full update path.
statusNote: Current recommended release for compatible DirectInput controllers.
highlights: Waits for the public latest update manifest to report the candidate version and tag before launching the unchanged v1.9.3 updater.
Bounds that wait to five minutes and records the last observed public manifest state if GitHub release metadata does not become ready.
Preserves all packaged mapper, controller, vJoy, DirectInput-to-vJoy report-path, installer, helper, and configuration-migration behavior from v2.0.5.
